note: A legato trill on fingers 2 and 3, the pair that likes to move together. The old tempo stages are now moves (80 to 104 bpm), named only as {{=bpm}}; the step names who plays (one pick, then the fretting hand alone), the feel to reach is the pull as loud as the hammer, and nothing names a selector.

exercise.title: Hammer and pull, fingers 2 and 3
exercise.why: A pulled-off note is sounded by the finger leaving the string, so a trill is only even when the pull is as firm as the hammer.

cells.text:
Press Play below to start the metronome at {{=bpm}}, and follow the tab. Pick the first note once, then hammer finger 3 on and pull it off to finger 2, one note per beat, with no more picking.
Pull finger 3 slightly sideways as it leaves, so it plucks the string for the next note.
Practice until the pulled-off note sounds as loud as the hammered one.
